statement:
For a topological group $G$, a **discrete continuous $G$-module** is an abelian group with the discrete topology and continuous left $G$-action, equivalently every element has open stabilizer. Let $\operatorname{Mod}_G$ be their abelian category. For a ring $R$, $\operatorname{Mod}_{R,G}$ consists of $R$-modules with compatible continuous **$R$-linear** $G$-action. Group cohomology $H^i(G,M)$ is the right-derived functor of the **invariants** $M^G$ on these categories, not the continuous-cochain cohomology of arbitrary nondiscrete topological modules. If $M$ is finite projective as an $R$-module, $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ has **contragredient** action $(g\lambda)(m)=\lambda(g^{-1}m)$, and $M^\vee\otimes_RN$ the diagonal action. $\operatorname{Ext}^i(M,N)$ is in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R,G}$.

**Standalone statement (original source hypotheses retained):**
Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $R$ be a ring.
For every $i \geq 0$ the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\text{Mod}_{R, G} \ar[rr]_{H^i(G, -)} \ar[d] & &
\text{Mod}_R \ar[d] \\
\text{Mod}_G \ar[rr]^{H^i(G, -)} & &
\textit{Ab}
}
$$
whose vertical arrows are the forgetful functors is commutative.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-dim-group-cohomology}
Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $k$ be a field.
Let $V$ be a $k\text{-}G$-module.
If $G$ is topologically finitely generated and
$\dim_k(V) < \infty$, then $\dim_k H^1(G, V) < \infty$.

For a topological group $G$, a **discrete continuous $G$-module** is an abelian group with the discrete topology and continuous left $G$-action, equivalently every element has open stabilizer. Let $\operatorname{Mod}_G$ be their abelian category. For a ring $R$, $\operatorname{Mod}_{R,G}$ consists of $R$-modules with compatible continuous **$R$-linear** $G$-action. Group cohomology $H^i(G,M)$ is the right-derived functor of the **invariants** $M^G$ on these categories, not the continuous-cochain cohomology of arbitrary nondiscrete topological modules. **Standalone statement (original source hypotheses retained):**
Let $G$ be a profinite topological group.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^i(G, M)$ is torsion for $i > 0$ and any $G$-module $M$, and
\item $H^i(G, M) = 0$ if $M$ is a $\mathbf{Q}$-vector space.
\end{enumerate}

**Typing and scope:** The coefficients are **discrete continuous** G-modules. Only positive cohomological degrees are torsion/zero; invariants in degree zero can survive.
